page: Amazon Web Services c7g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton3 processors. It features 64 physical ARM64 cores based on the Neoverse-V1 architecture, operating at 2.6 GHz with a dedicated core allocation and no simultaneous multithreading. The instance is equipped with 128 GB of DDR5 memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 30 Gbps. No local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware is bundled with this instance.

In benchmark evaluations, the c7g.16xlarge demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench multi-core performance and software compilation with Clang. Memory subsystem performance is highly rated, with Passmark memory scores and uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching the top 10% and 25% thresholds respectively. Multi-core CPU stress tests and database operations, including Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput, also rank in the top 25%. However, single-core execution and text generation for small LLM models represent relative bottlenecks, falling into average and weak performance tiers.

The ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and power efficiency, translating to a favorable qualitative cost-to-performance ratio for multi-threaded workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. However, the lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which may impact I/O-heavy workloads. The absence of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX or AMX is a notable tradeoff for certain legacy applications. This instance is suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and medium-scale language model inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7g.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance featuring 64 dedicated ARM64 physical cores powered by AWS Graviton3 (Neoverse-V1) processors running at 2.6 GHz. It includes 128 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and runs on the Nitro hypervisor with 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data highlights top-tier multi-core CPU performance, software compilation speeds, and memory bandwidth, alongside strong database and static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core execution and small-model text generation benchmarks are average to weak. Given its high multi-core efficiency and lack of local storage, the c7g.16xlarge is suited for distributed multi-threaded workloads, containerized microservices, software development pipelines, and memory-bandwidth-sensitive database operations.
